oneOf.description:
The session's agent workflow exists but failed during bootstrap
(rehydration) and cannot serve runs. Distinct from `NotFound` (no
workflow) so clients/bridges treat it as a session recovery problem
rather than an ordinary "answer this message" failure.

The environment exists but is not reachable yet: it is still
provisioning/booting, or it was powered down and a wake (desired
power `running`) has been initiated by this request. Distinct from
`Rejected` so clients retry with backoff instead of failing —
polling and automation callers lean on this for wake-on-use.

The requested page still exceeds the public serialized response
budget. Callers can retry with a smaller page limit or continuation.

environment.description:

applied: activate an existing universe environment, or provision a
fresh one for this session. Absence leaves the session's current
active environment unchanged.

metadata.description:

Applying the profile to an existing session does not change metadata.

retention.description:

manual deletion. Applying a profile to an existing session does not
change retention.

AuthClientCreateParams.description:
Register an OAuth client configuration. `client_secret` is the second
deliberate inbound-plaintext path after `auth/grants/import`: it is
encrypted on receipt and never returned by any method. `Debug` output
redacts it; request logging must never echo these params.

authorizeUrl.description:
Authorization URL the user must open. It embeds the one-time `state`;
treat it as sensitive and do not log it server-side.

AuthGrantImportParams.description:
Import a static bearer credential as an auth grant. This is the one
deliberate inbound-plaintext path: `token` is encrypted on receipt and is
never returned by any method. `Debug` output redacts the token; request
logging must never echo these params.

metadata.description:
Non-secret, caller-defined metadata stored on the grant and returned
by reads (for example which product a pasted subscription token
belongs to). Must be a JSON object; never put secret material here.

AuthGrantLeaseParams.description:
Request a current access-token lease for a retrievable grant. Callers must
cache only in memory until shortly before `expiresAtMs` (or for at most
five minutes when it is absent), re-lease after target 401/403 responses,
and never persist the token or place it in a workflow payload.

metadata.description:
Non-secret provider-specific metadata (for GitHub App installation
grants: installation id, account, permissions, repository selection).

oneOf.description:
Stored model provider API key; the key arrives via `credential` and is
encrypted on receipt.

Bind an existing auth grant as a model provider credential. No
`credential` is accepted; the grant's tokens stay in the grant store.
Register an endpoint that requires no provider credential.

AuthProviderConfigView.description:
Non-secret, provider-specific configuration. New providers add a
variant, not a table.

oneOf.description:
Stored model provider API key (`model:<provider_id>` rows). The key itself
is the provider credential and never appears in views.

OAuth-grant-backed model provider credential: provider calls send the
bound grant's access token as an OAuth bearer token.
Credentialless OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

AuthProviderCreateParams.description:
Register an auth provider. `credential` (for GitHub Apps: the private
key PEM) is the third deliberate inbound-plaintext path: it is encrypted
on receipt and never returned by any method. `Debug` output redacts it;
request logging must never echo these params.

BlobPutParams.description:
`blobs/put` is batch-native: pass one item to store a single blob. Results
come back in request order. Uploads are eligible for collection after the
deployment's grace period unless retained by a durable resource. Reads do
not extend retention; admitting an existing ref refreshes its grace.

BotBreaker.description:

events inside `window_ms` is disabled until a human re-enables it.

triggers.description:

CitationView.description:
A source the assistant cited, in the same shape for every provider. The
exact provider output stays in a separate opaque context entry for replay.

ContentRefView.description:
Immutable content and its encoding. A reference can name plain text,
provider-native JSON, or media; it does not imply a UTF-8 text payload.

key.description:
Stable client-chosen context key. Re-sending the same key with the
same content is a no-op, so the key doubles as the idempotency handle.
`run`, `run.*`, `runtime`, and `runtime.*` are reserved for the runtime.

activationTextTruncated.description:
True when `activation_text` was cut off at the server-side length cap.
The committed context entry always holds the full text.

origin.description:
Application-supplied display origin, independent of role and insertion source.
`user:<id>` identifies platform composer input; `event` marks bot deliveries.
Other values are allowed; omission means unknown. Not an authorization identity.

provenanceRef.description: Immutable artifact recording this entry's origin or construction.

oneOf.description: Runtime or client catalog with a stored text body and independent key.

ContextEntryView.description:
A session context entry, faithful to the stored engine entry: keyed,
kind-tagged, ref-backed. Keys are a stable extension point — clients
reconstruct derived surfaces (e.g. the prompted instruction set via the
`prompt_instructions/` key prefix) by filtering on `key` and fetching
original bytes through `blobs/read`. `text` contains complete message and
visible reasoning text; tool and catalog bodies use bounded text previews.

citations.description:
Sources this assistant message cites, derived from its own native
payload. Empty for every other entry kind.

origin.description:
Application-supplied display origin, independent of role and insertion source.
`user:<id>` identifies platform composer input; `event` marks bot deliveries.
Other values are allowed; omission means unknown. Not an authorization identity.

provenanceRef.description: Immutable artifact recording this entry's origin or construction.

providerItemId.description: Native item identity derived from the payload, when present.

source.description:
Where the entry came from: run input, a steering batch, model output,
a tool result, reasoning state, a context edit, or the runtime. Lets
transcripts render steering distinctly from the run's first input.

supersededBy.description:
For a catalog entry that a newer version has updated: that newer
entry. Present only on state views (`session/read`), where the whole
active context is known.

supersedes.description:
For a catalog entry: the earlier version of the same keyed catalog
that this entry updates. The earlier entry stays in context until a
rewrite drops it.

textTruncated.description:
True when a tool or catalog body's `text` is a bounded prefix. Fetch
its original content through `blobs/read`. Messages and reasoning are full.

keys.description:
Active context keys to remove. Removing a key that is already absent
is a per-key no-op (`absent`), so retries are idempotent. Keys under
reserved namespaces (`run`, `run.*`, `runtime`, `runtime.*`) are rejected
request-level.

idlePolicy.description: Optional staged idle policy applied by the power reaper.

requestId.description: Stable caller-generated retry identity, unique inside the universe.

The environment daemon (`lightspeed-envd`) that belongs to a server
release. Download locations and checksums are not here: the deployment
publishes them in its discovery document, outside the authenticated API.

protocolVersion.description:
Environment protocol version the gateway speaks. A daemon registers
only when it reports exactly this number.

targets.description: Rust target triples the daemon is published for.

connection.description: Connection to an envd instance reachable from Lightspeed.

EnvironmentIdentityModeView.description:
What Lightspeed does with a registered environment while its daemon is
disconnected. Registration-key policy, copied onto each environment.

oneOf.description: Stays offline until explicitly closed.

Closed once the daemon has been away longer than the key's
disconnect grace.

idlePolicy.description: The complete new policy; omit to clear it.

EnvironmentIdlePolicyView.description:
Staged idle policy. Thresholds are milliseconds of daemon-reported idle
time and must be non-decreasing in the order pause, suspend, stop, close.
Stages whose power state the provider does not support are skipped.

powerStates.description:
Power states the provider reported for this target; empty until
observed or when the provider offers no power control.

oneOf.description: Execution frozen; wakes on next use.
Execution state saved to disk; wakes on next use.

provider supports power control.

providers.description: Absent means every registered provider is allowed.

workflow-backed tools.

deleteAfterCloseMs.description:
Root-owned automatic deletion measured from close. Absent inherits a
profile default, explicit null keeps the tree, and a duration overrides
the profile.

environment.description:
Optional creation-time override for the selected profile's environment
intent. Omit to use the profile's intent unchanged.

metadata.description:
Descriptive key/value metadata with the same bounds as
`session/start`; applied only when the session is first created.

workflowTools.description:
Immutable workflow tools admitted only when the session is first
created. This document is not part of `SessionConfig` and cannot be
changed through `session/config/put`.

McpFeature.description:
Grants remote MCP tools by declaring linked servers from the universe MCP
catalog; must link at least one server, with unique server ids.

scopesSupported.description:
Scopes advertised by current protected-resource/authorization-server
metadata. Advisory only; clients must not silently expand consent.

McpServerAuthDiscoverParams.description:
Read-only authentication discovery for a prospective MCP endpoint. A
missing OAuth result is deliberately inconclusive: the server may be
public, use bearer auth, or expose OAuth metadata only through an explicit
URL. No catalog or auth records are created by this probe.

McpServerCredential.description:
Non-secret universe credential selected by this configured MCP server.
Token material remains in the auth subsystem and is never returned.

McpServerInput.description: Full MCP server document as submitted by clients.

McpServerLink.description:
A selected universe MCP server. Its catalog record owns all connection and
behavior configuration.

expectedRevision.description:
Checked only when the server already exists; absent replaces (or
creates) unconditionally.

McpServerToolsDiscoverParams.description: Live, non-persisting tool discovery for a configured MCP server.

McpToolAnnotationsView.description:
Narrow projection of standard MCP `ToolAnnotations`. All values are
untrusted hints and never authorization facts.

parallelToolUse.description: Omitted when the provider model-list API does not report this fact.

ModelListParams.description:
Direct provider model discovery. Results may be served from a brief
process-local cache; clients refresh by calling this method.

selectableOnly.description:
Apply Lightspeed's small, conservative selectable-model policy. It
removes OpenAI model-id families that are clearly not text-generation
routes (embeddings, moderation, image/video, speech, and realtime).
It is an ID policy, not a provider capability claim.

ModelProcessingTier.description: Provider processing class used by session defaults and per-run overrides.

oneOf.description: A universe-owned `model:<provider>` credential.
The deployment-wide fallback key from server configuration.

A credential was found and was not rejected by the provider (other
discovery errors, e.g. transport, may still be reported).
No credential anywhere: no universe row and no deployment fallback.

A credential exists but is unusable (disabled/legacy universe row) or
was rejected by the provider (HTTP 401/403).

The universe provider row explicitly configures an unauthenticated
endpoint, so no credential is expected.

ModelProviderDiscoveryView.description:
Best-effort status for one provider. A provider failure does not discard
models discovered from other providers.

credential.description:
Whether a usable credential exists for this provider — a stable signal
for clients (no string matching on `error`).

credentialSource.description: Where the credential used for this universe comes from.

error.description:
Sanitized Lightspeed error; never a credential, request header, or raw
upstream response body.

ModelView.description: A model route returned directly by a provider API.

apiKind.description: Canonical Lightspeed provider API kind, e.g. `openai:responses`.

createdAtMs.description:
Provider-reported model creation time. Omitted when the provider does
not expose one; this is distinct from the discovery fetch time.

source.description: Always `provider`; there is no maintained model catalog.

displayName.description: Human-readable purpose shown in key-management interfaces.

principal.description:
Audit principal applied to grants and flows created through this key.
This does not grant platform/operator authority.

OperatorApiKeyCreateResponse.description:
A newly minted key. `secret` is returned only by create and cannot be
recovered later. Its custom `Debug` implementation redacts the DTO before
JSON-RPC serialization; the serialized response payload remains sensitive
and must not be logged.

OperatorApiKeyView.description:
Non-secret API-key metadata. The owning universe is supplied by every
request and intentionally omitted from entries so list responses cannot
become a deployment-wide tenant catalog by accident.

includeDisabled.description: Include disabled accounts; by default only enabled ones are listed.

OperatorChannelAccountView.description:
One channel account of any universe, for the connector host's discovery
pass.

credentialGrantId.description:
Retrievable auth grant holding the provider token (a Telegram bot
token); the connector host leases it. Absent for providers whose
credential is a session state directory (WhatsApp).

providerAccountId.description:
Provider-native account identity: the Telegram bot username or
numeric id, the WhatsApp phone number. Unique per universe and
provider.

requestId.description: Stable caller-generated retry identity inside the destination universe.

sourceTarget.description:
Provider-native source reference. The Incus provider accepts
`<project>/<instance>` or an instance name in the `default` project.

takeOwnership.description:
Required acknowledgement that Lightspeed will move, reconfigure, and
delete the target as part of its ordinary managed lifecycle.

created.description: False when the universe already existed (create is idempotent).

OperatorUniverseDeleteResponse.description:
Purge report. The purge is idempotent: rerunning after a partial failure
resumes where it stopped, and the universe row is deleted last so a
half-purged universe is still visible to `operator/universes/read`.

blobObjectsDeleted.description: External object-store blobs deleted during the purge.

workflowsTerminated.description: Live session workflows terminated during the purge.

OperatorUniverseView.description:
Per-universe stats view. Counts are cheap aggregates computed at read
time, not maintained counters — approximate under concurrent writes.

lastActivityAtMs.description:
Most recent session activity (`max(sessions.updated_at_ms)`); absent
when the universe has no sessions.

PollCursorSpec.description:
Dedupe discipline of a poll: an id set for unordered feeds, a watermark
for ordered ones.

oneOf.description: Dot path to each item's id.
Dot path to each item's monotonically increasing field.

PollCursorState.description:
Poll cursor state: Lightspeed-owned, operator-visible, reset by a spec
edit. Absent until the baseline poll.

PollHttpAuth.description:
Leased credential for an HTTP poll source; the value never appears in
the trigger document.

scheme.description: Scheme prefix; default `Bearer`, empty sends the token raw.

PollSource.description: Where a poll trigger reads from.

headers.description: Non-secret headers only; credentials come from `auth`.

environmentId.description:
Universe environment the command runs in (woken on use); absent
runs in the bot's own environment (the profile's `existing`
one), resolved at fire time.

timeoutMs.description: Job wall-clock budget; also bounds the fire activity's wait.

environmentProvisioned.description: True when this apply created a new environment for the session.

ProfileEnvironment.description: Environment intent carried by a profile document.

oneOf.description:
Activate an existing universe environment. The profile never closes
it.

Activate the delegating parent's active environment. Resolved at
sub-agent spawn, shared not copied, never closed by the
child; rejected on a session without a delegation origin or whose
parent has no active environment.

Provision one environment for the session from the universe's enabled
binding for `providerId`, then activate it. The provision request id
is derived from the session id, so retries and repeated applies
converge on the same environment.

credentials.description:
Credentials bound to the environment right after it is
provisioned before activation: references to universe
grants/providers/secrets, never values. They become ordinary
environment credential bindings; the profile is the initial set,
not a live sync. Not available for `existing` environments.

idlePolicy.description:
Optional staged idle policy for the provisioned environment.
Stages the provider cannot realize are skipped.

ProfileEnvironmentCredential.description:
One environment credential binding requested by a profile: the same shape
as `environments/credentials/bind`.

ProfileEnvironmentRetention.description:
What happens to a profile-provisioned environment when its originating
session closes.

oneOf.description: Close the environment when the session that provisioned it closes.
Leave the environment open; the universe owns its cleanup.

Borrowed CAS content: saving a profile does not retain the blob. Use
inline text, or keep this ref retained by another durable resource.

expectedRevision.description:
Checked only when the profile already exists; absent replaces (or
creates) unconditionally.

ProfileSessionRetention.description: Root-session retention policy supplied by a profile at session creation.

RunFailureKindView.description: Why a run failed, as the engine classified it.

cursor.description: Exclusive upper run-id bound from a previous page.

RunReadResponse.description:
The complete projection of one run. Run projection is stateful across the
run's events, so partial pages would silently lose cross-event state; a
run whose interval exceeds the server's detail ceiling is rejected with a
typed error and remains readable through `session/events/read`. Inline
message and reasoning text is complete. Tool and catalog previews are bounded;
their full bodies remain available through `blobs/read`.

notifyOnTerminal.description:
Request an at-least-once terminal emission to the managed session's
immutable lifecycle controller. The destination is derived by the
gateway; callers supply only the controller's opaque dedup token.

submissionId.description:
Client-supplied idempotency key, unique per session. Retrying
`session/runs/start` with the same submission id and the same
source/config/terminal notification returns the original run instead
of starting a second one; reusing a submission id with any of those
inputs changed is rejected.

items.description:
Steering input, same vocabulary as run input. Delivered to the model
at the next turn boundary of the run; it does not interrupt the
in-flight turn or wake a parked await.

runId.description:
The run to steer. Must be the session's current active run (running
or parked on an await); a finished or cancelling run is rejected so a
late steer never lands on the next run.

steeringId.description: Identifier of the accepted steering batch within the session.

RunSummaryView.description:
Bounded run metadata projected from reducer state. Transcript entries and
tool payloads are available only from `session/runs/read` or the event
stream.

completedAtMs.description:
When the run reached a terminal state, derived from its committed
completed, failed, or cancelled event. Absent for non-terminal runs.

output.description: Authoritative terminal output, retained independently of active context.

outputText.description:
Complete visible text derived from `output`; absent for non-text output
or runs without a terminal output. Native metadata stays in the blob.

startedAtMs.description:
When the run left the queue and began executing, derived from the
committed `runStarted` event. Absent while the run is queued.

envd.description:
The environment daemon build this release ships. Descriptive: the
gateway admits any daemon that speaks `envd.protocolVersion`,
whatever commit it was built from.

gitSha.description: Full git commit this server was built from.

version.description:
Release version with the git commit as SemVer build metadata, for
example `0.1.0+2093b949…`.

force.description:
Cancel the active run and drop queued runs instead of rejecting on
active work. Recovers sessions whose workflow no longer exists (e.g.
after an operator terminate) by reconciling the session log directly.

SessionConfig.description:
Declared session configuration document.

Sparse and capability-oriented: an omitted section means defaults, an
absent feature is not granted (no tools, no access). The document is
replaced whole via `session/config/put`; reads return exactly the stored
document, so read-modify-write round-trips.

model.description:
Absent on input means the deployment default model. Documents read
back from a session always carry the model; the provider api kind is
pinned for the session's lifetime.

SessionConfigPutParams.description:
Replace the session config with a complete document. Anything omitted
from the document reverts to defaults; an absent feature is revoked.
Requires an idle session; putting an identical document is a no-op that
leaves the revision untouched.

expectedConfigRevision.description:
Checked against the session's current config revision when present;
absent replaces unconditionally.

cascade.description:
Delete history forks and delegated descendants too. False requires the
target to be a closed retention-tree leaf.

SessionEnvironmentOverride.description:
Creation-time override for the environment intent carried by a profile.
Absence uses the profile unchanged; `none` suppresses its environment
intent, while `existing` activates the specified universe environment.

oneOf.description:
One system-owned workflow-backed tool was durably admitted without
assigning lifecycle ownership to the session.

completionPromises.description:
Keyed completion promises created atomically with the
invocation; absent for notify-only (accepted) invocations.

oneOf.description:
Durable start intent for a start-on-call workflow tool. There is no
successful started event; the deterministic execution id makes the
start replay-safe.

completionPromises.description:
Keyed completion promises created atomically with the start
intent.

executionId.description:
System-derived deterministic execution id of the started plugin
workflow.

oneOf.description:
The run ended in failure. `kind` is the engine's classification;
`message` is free text for display.

usage.description:
Provider token usage for this generation, including the
prompt-cache read/write counts, when the provider reported it.

oneOf.description:
The run was cancelled while this turn was open; the turn ended without
a generation result.

One tool call finished. `output_bytes` is the size of the
model-visible text the tool produced before the runtime's projection
budget was applied, absent for synthetic results; `truncated` is true
when that budget cut it.

before.description: Exclusive upper sequence bound for backward reads only. Must be positive.

direction.description:
Forward reads follow `after`; backward reads select the latest window
below `before` (or the current head when absent). Both return events
chronologically. Backward reads do not replay reducer state.

waitMs.description:
Forward reads only. Long-poll: when no events exist past `after`, hold the request until
one lands or this many milliseconds elapse, then return a normal
(possibly empty) page. Zero or absent preserves immediate return.
Values above the server cap are clamped, not rejected.

complete.description:
No more events in the requested direction at the time of this read.
This does not imply that the session is closed.

events.description:
Events are always chronological, including backward pages. A page may
begin inside a run or tool batch; clients must retain continuation state.

headCursor.description:
Backward reads fence the head before reading. The initial backward
page's head is the starting `after` cursor for live forward reads.
An empty backward read returns sequence zero.

nextCursor.description:
Forward: pass as `after`. Backward: pass as `before` to fetch older
history; absent when the beginning is reached. Never use a backward
continuation to advance a forward live cursor.

orphanedDescendants.description:
True when the job's root process exited while descendants it spawned
were still running; the host terminated them best-effort at job
completion.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `nextCursor`.

excludeClosed.description:
Exclude closed sessions. New sessions that have not run yet remain in
the result alongside open sessions.

metadata.description:
Only sessions matching every entry (AND semantics). A non-empty value
requires an exact key/value pair; an empty value requires key presence.
Combines with the lineage filters.

parentSessionId.description: Only sub-agent sessions delegated directly by this session.

rootSessionId.description: Only sub-agent sessions whose lineage root is this session.

nextCursor.description:
Present when more sessions exist past this page. Ordering is most
recently updated first; pages can drift under concurrent activity.

SessionMetadataPutParams.description:
Replace a session's metadata with a complete map (the same bounds as
`session/start`). Record-only: it does not touch the event log or
`updatedAtMs`. There is no merge form; read, edit, and put.

metadata.description: The complete new map; empty clears it.

SessionMutationView.description:
Compact acknowledgement returned by session mutations. Call
`session/read` when the complete current-state summary is needed.

SessionOriginView.description:
Typed provenance of a delegated (sub-agent) session: who created it,
under which root, at what depth, and the effective limits it was spawned
with. Provenance, never ownership — the child is an ordinary session.

depth.description: Absolute depth from the root; a root's direct child is 1.

invocationId.description: The workflow-tool invocation that created the child.

rootSessionId.description:
Nearest ancestor without an origin; root-scoped limits count every
session naming this root.

runLimit.description:
Newest run summaries to include. Values above the server maximum are
clamped.

displayName.description: New display name; absent clears it.

deleteAfterCloseMs.description: Positive duration enables automatic tree deletion; null disables it.

SessionRetentionView.description:
Effective tree-owned retention for a session. Forks and delegated children
name their owning root and project that root's policy and deadline.

deleteAfterCloseMs.description:
Root-owned automatic deletion measured from close. Absent inherits a
profile default, explicit null keeps the tree, and a duration overrides
the profile.

environment.description:
Optional creation-time override for the selected profile's environment
intent. Omit to use the profile's intent unchanged.

metadata.description:
Descriptive key/value metadata, applied only when the session is
first created: at most 32 entries, keys 1..=64 bytes, values 1..=256
bytes, no control characters, no `lightspeed.` prefix. It never
affects routing, authority, or selection; filter on it with
`session/list`.

managed.description:
True only when immutable lifecycle ownership was admitted with a
lifecycle controller at managed-session creation.

metadata.description: Descriptive key/value metadata; empty when none was set.

origin.description: Sub-agent lineage; absent for root sessions.

activeEnvironmentId.description: The universe environment selected by the session event log.

activeRun.description:
The currently executing run, always present when one exists — the
paged `runs` window can omit it behind newer queued runs, so control
surfaces (steering, status) must read it from here.

config.description:
The stored sparse config document, exactly as last put (model and
feature versions materialized at admission). Effective tool reality
is visible via `active_tools`.

managed.description:
True only when immutable lifecycle ownership was admitted with a
lifecycle controller at managed-session creation.

management.description:
Immutable workflow-backed tool declaration. A lifecycle controller
indicates external session ownership; tool-only declarations do not.

metadata.description: Descriptive key/value metadata; empty when none was set.

origin.description: Sub-agent lineage; absent for root sessions.

SkillCatalogView.description: An independent catalog instance; sources are never merged or used as fallbacks.

location.description: Where to read the instructions and resolve supporting files.

SkillLocationView.description: Readable paths within the owning catalog's filesystem domain.

SubagentAgentPin.description: The profile a sub-agent was spawned from, pinned at its revision.

SubagentsFeature.description:
Grants sub-agent delegation: `agent_run` (joined, result inline) and
`agent_spawn` (promise, joined with `await`) over the listed agent
profiles. Limits are root-scoped and attenuating: every descendant of a
root session counts against the root, and a nested grant can narrow but
never widen the limits pinned on its origin.

agents.description:
The agent menu. Every id must name an existing profile; the model
picks by id and reads descriptions from the sub-agent catalog.

deadlineMs.description:
Per-child run deadline in milliseconds; at most the execution
ceiling of 24 hours.

maxConcurrent.description: Open sessions under the root at any time, excluding the root.

maxDepth.description: A child at depth `d` may spawn only while `d + 1 <= maxDepth`.

maxDescendants.description: Lifetime total of sessions ever created under the root.

TimersFeature.description:
Grants timer promises through the sleep tool plus the base concurrency
tools (await/cancel/detach).

toolId.description: Admitted registry identity, absent when the model used an unavailable name.

completedAtMs.description:
When the call's terminal result was committed. The window to
`startedAtMs` includes runtime scheduling overhead.

durationMs.description:
Execution milliseconds measured by the runtime around the call body;
the remainder of the started/completed window is overhead.

startedAtMs.description:
When the call was dispatched for execution, from the committed
`toolCallStarted` event. Absent until dispatch.

toolId.description: Admitted registry identity, absent when the model used an unavailable name.

oneOf.description: Code-owned definition; names and schemas are resolved for each turn.

VfsFeature.description:
Grants the session virtual filesystem. Workspace links declare the
session-visible namespace and the VFS catalog is surfaced. Sub-grants are independent; `{}` grants a VFS with
no tools and no sourcing.

prompts.description:
Prompt-instruction sourcing from the VFS. Absent disables loading;
an empty block discovers conventional linked roots.

skills.description:
Independent VFS skill discovery. Absent disables discovery and removes
its runtime catalog; an empty block discovers conventional linked roots.

tools.description:
Agent-facing filesystem tool surface; absent = no fs tools. Per-path
writability is defined by each workspace link's own access.
With the environments feature granted, `readOnly` also exposes
`vfs_materialize`; `edit` additionally exposes `vfs_capture`.
Prompt/skill sourcing alone does not grant transfer tools.

workspaceLinks.description: Catalog resources exposed in the session's workspace namespace.

roots.description:
Absent searches .agents/prompts and .lightspeed/prompts beneath each
workspace link. Explicit roots replace these defaults and must be
non-empty absolute paths contained in workspace links.

Absent searches .agents/skills and .lightspeed/skills beneath each
workspace link. Explicit roots replace these defaults and must be
non-empty absolute paths contained in workspace links.

snapshotRef.description:
Snapshot to seed the workspace from. Absent starts the workspace from
the empty snapshot, committed server-side.

bytes.description: Total byte size of the head snapshot.

files.description: File count of the head snapshot.

WebFeature.description:
Grants network access through the web toolset; `fetch` and `search` are
independently granted, and a web block granting neither is rejected.

allowedDomains.description: Absent means all domains; an explicit list must be non-empty.

WebhookVerification.description:
How an inbound webhook proves it comes from the sender: possession of
the URL token, or additionally an HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body with a
secret leased from a retrievable grant.

WorkflowStartRefInput.description:
Opaque reference to a workflow-substrate recipe already stored through
the blob API. The fingerprint authenticates the exact recipe bytes used
by the workflow-start adapter.

WorkflowToolCompletionInput.description:
Completion contract for one workflow-tool invocation. Joined tools park
the original call on one runtime-owned reply; Promises exposes handles for
model-controlled concurrency.

WorkflowToolCompletionKeySourceInput.description: Declarative promise-key derivation over schema-validated tool arguments.

oneOf.description: The single reserved `reply` key.
A JSON Pointer to an array of unique completion-key strings.

A JSON Pointer to an array of objects; the named string field of
every item is its completion key, so the model's own name for a work
item keys that item's promise.

A JSON Pointer to an array; keys are `prefix` joined with each item's
zero-based index.

name.description: Function name exposed to the model and used as its registry identity.

WorkflowToolTargetInput.description:
Lifecycle target of a workflow-backed tool. Bound tools deliver to an
existing execution; start tools create an execution from an immutable,
CAS-backed recipe for every invocation.

description: All JSON-RPC wire types of the Lightspeed agent API.
